public_source.paper_title: New lower bound on the Shannon capacity of C7 from circular graphs
public_source.evidence: The paper's abstract states an independent set of size 367 in the fifth strong product power of C7. The task-local witness is transcribed from the construction and appendix and checked by the exact task checker.

survey_cross_checks.evidence: The repository describes the global bounds as 367 <= alpha(C7^5) <= 401, states that its September 2026 work found no 368-word construction, and preserves the scope and limits of its certificates.
The page identifies the Polak-Schrijver 367 construction as the previous SOTA. Its displayed agent submissions score 366; no larger valid construction is listed on the checked page.

The published AlphaEvolve problem catalog describes 67 problems; a C7 fifth-power independent-set result was not identified in that catalog. This is a catalog check, not a claim about unpublished or private runs.

The checked SimpleTES task and released-result listings did not identify a C7^5 task or a stronger same-parameter construction. DREAM-RSI's public repository says its mathematics tasks are fetched from SimpleTES; its checked task listing did not identify this problem either.
The public repository identifies SimpleTES as the source of its mathematics task packages. Its checked launch/task listing did not identify an T011-equivalent C7^5 run or witness.

verification.source_review: Sol checked Polak–Schrijver fifth-power parameters and 367-word result, replayed the saved set, independently checked all 67,161 pairs and rejected duplicate words. A stronger same-parameter witness was not found in the checked public sources.

limitations: This is a verified lower bound, not a proof that 367 is optimal; the cited contemporary survey records the upper bound 401.
2026 constructions improve lower bounds for the Shannon capacity using higher strong powers of C7. Those results do not give a larger independent set in this fixed fifth power.

The public-source comparison covers the cited paper, the checked 2026 C7^5 research repository and challenge page, and the public AlphaEvolve, SimpleTES, and DREAM-RSI task listings. It cannot exclude private, unpublished, or later results.

public_source.paper_title: Improved lower bound on Shannon capacity of C7
public_source.evidence: The article reports an independent set of size 108 found by simulated annealing and asks whether alpha(C7^4)>108; it gives no optimality proof. The checked public archive has no machine-readable transcription suitable for exact replay.

human_reference.method: Cartesian square of a 10-word C7^2 independent set

limitations: Vesel–Žerovnik report 108 for this same configuration, but this package does not claim to reproduce the figure-based construction.
Itty et al. (2026), §2 states alpha(C7^4) is unknown and alpha(C7^4) >=108; optimality is open.

public_source.paper_title: Improved lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of odd cycles
public_source.evidence: The paper and pinned author repository publish a 1120-word C7^6 independent set. The abstract states that the construction was discovered through iterative LLM interaction, so provenance is AI-assisted.

human_reference.method: Cartesian product of the published human 367-word C7^5 witness and the traditional single-cycle set {0,2,4}; independent set product theorem.

limitations: The 1120 construction is AI-assisted, not a human-only construction.
The local human comparator is the traditional 1101 product; it does not replace the stronger public record.
This is a verified lower bound and not a proof of optimality.
